Name: Elena Gold
Question: Why are the Russians targeting residential areas in Ukraine?
Answer: A captain of a Russian ship confessed targeting residential buildings: “If it’s a 5-storey building, then we aim at the entrance. If it doesn’t hit this one, then it will definitely hit some other building in the neighborhood.” He said the precision of the strikes is “within inches”. So, Russians themselves admit what they are doing. Russian military bloggers reveal why they are doing it: because they want to make Ukrainians surrender, because Russia can’t “win” otherwise. Targeting residential buildings is a completely deliberate strategy. Weirdly, there are still some people in the West buying Russia’s excuses.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is it true that wages in Russia are very low and the cost of living is very high?
Answer: A young Russian policewoman was fired for posting a reel on Instagram where she mocked her $400 (40,000 rub.) monthly salary, which is actually less than $100 per week. (Video in the comments below.) 28-year-old Olga Gaidukova worked as a district police officer in the town of Novocherkassk (Rostov region), population 160,000, which is in the South of Russia, near the Ukrainian border. The satiric reel about her salary, which she published in her personal Instagram account, scored a lot of views and likes. It is this popularity that got her in trouble. Reportedly, the young lady was called to her superiors, who demanded from her to delete the Instagram account — but she refused and was fired. The defiant ex-police officer admitted that she didn’t think her bosses would go that far. There aren’t too many willing candidates for such jobs and police officers are overworked. The cost of living keeps skyrocketing. Mortgage rates are at 17% in Russia, and the government just cancelled special rates for first home buyers (which were at 8%). “Prices are cheaper than they will be tomorrow!” — Russians bitterly joke about the constantly rising prices. The Russian central bank plans to raise the base rate, which is currently at 16%, so the mortgage rates could be going beyond the scary 17% per year already this month. Putin keeps saying that Russians can purchase more goods with their low salaries than westerners can buy with their much higher wages, but I don’t think many westerners would want to live on the ration of cabbage soup with bread and tea with cookies. This is actually what pensioners in Russia eat every day, because most of their pension money they spend on utilities bills (aka “kommunalka”). After paying for their homes, they can only spend $1–3 per day on food. And no, it’s not enough to buy proper food. Yes, Russian people working regular jobs live better than homeless people in America living in the streets. But they don’t live anywhere as comfortable as Americans who work in the same type of jobs. That’s a fact.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Is Russia behind the global cyber attack?
Answer: CrowdStrike, the cybersecurity company behind the global outage today, stated that the problems were caused by an update to their software. The company has over 20,000 businesses worldwide, including major banks, airports, TV broadcasters and supermarket chains. An update to CrowdStrike’s "Falcon Sensor" software was causing Microsoft Windows to crash and display a blue screen (aka "Blue Screen of Death"). George Kurtz, CrowdStrike's CEO, announced that the company provided a fix for the issue and assured that it was "not a security incident or cyberattack.” “A defect found in a single content update for Windows hosts” caused all the trouble. Max and Linux hosts weren’t affected. A little piece of bad code — and the world is in shock, fearing a global cyber attack. Russia, of course, would love to take the credit — but no, this one we did to ourselves.

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Do you think Russia will ever hand over Sergei K. Shoigu and Gen. Valery V. Gerasimov to the International Criminal Court?
Answer: To celebrate 1-year anniversary of Prigozhin’s rebellion, The Hague International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Sergei Shoigu, former minister of defence of Russia, and Valery Gerasimov, Chief of General Staff. Now, not only Putin and children’s ombudsman Maria Lvova-Belova are on the list of international war criminals, but the top guys who commanded the troops to attack Ukraine, are being wanted in Hague for shelling civilians. Sergei Shoigu was removed from his job of the minister of defence in May 2024, and given the nominal position the secretary of Russia’s security council; Valery Gerasimov remains the chief of general staff. Handing war criminals to prosecution is a requirement of Ukraine’s Peace Plan. This will be surely a requirement to lift western sanctions from Russia, which became the most sanctioned country in the world after its treacherous attack on Ukraine in February 2022, surpassing Iran and North Korea. And this is why, after Putin’s sudden death, Russia will gleefully hand all the war criminals to Hague, to get rid of the sanctions. Meanwhile, in Makhachkala, Dagestan, masked militants with guns are again walking in the streets. Residents shared home videos from Korkmasova Street: armed police officers take positions, there are shootouts in streets. In Makhachkala, security forces blocked off a square in the city center. (Video in the comments below.) After June 23 attacks on churches and synagogues, Dagestan’s authorities accused (surprise, surprise) America in organizing the attacks, “to split the unity of the Russian people”. Today, there is more unrest — and the attackers are well-equipped. There were expectations that Caucasus would inflame amidst Russia’s war in Ukraine, and it’s not the first time that Dagestan is in the news because of unrest since February 2022. But previous mass protests in Dagestan didn’t involve armed militants and shootouts with the police. Could these be the groups that complete what Yevgeny Prigozhin started on June 23, 2023, and march all the way to Moscow?

Name: Elena Gold
Question: Was Stalin really that bad, or was he a victim of propaganda?
Answer: In 1930s, young Mikhail Sholokhov was already a known author in the USSR for his book “Tales of the Don” (1925), depicting his personal experiences during the WWI, the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and the Civil War. When Stalin’s attack on peasants with the goal of shoveling them into “collective farms” began, Sholokhov lived in the village of Veshenskaya, Rostov region, and could see what was happening with the people. Witnessing the deaths and suffering of peasants, Sholokhov wrote 4 letters to Stalin in hopes of saving people. April 20, 1932: “I saw something that cannot be forgotten till my last days: at night, in the Volokhovsky village of the Lebyazhensky collective farm, in the fierce wind, in the freezing cold, when even dogs were hiding from the frosty weather, families of peasants who were thrown out of their houses had been burning fires in the alleys and sitting near the flames. Children were wrapped in rags and laid on the bare ground, thawed by the fire. A continuous children’s cry stood over the alleys. Why are people being tortured like that? In the Bazkovsky collective farm, a woman with a baby was evicted from her home. She was walking around the village all night, asking to be allowed to warm up with her child. Nobody let her in, fearing that if they do, they themselves would be evicted. By morning, the child froze to death in his mother's arms...” Stalin replied that Sholokhov simply lacked the class consciousness. Yes, Stalin was absolutely evil. It’s not just “propaganda”.
